deviations.what: FairDMFilterBackend now replaces django-filter's DjangoFilterBackend in REST_FRAMEWORK DEFAULT_FILTER_BACKENDS, and its built-filter-set cache is keyed by model as well.
deviations.why: Projects, datasets and contributors have no filter set and use the default backends, so this is the one place every list goes through.

concerns: fairdm/core/measurement/config.py:71: BaseMeasurementConfiguration sets description = 'Observation or calculation recorded from a sample', so for any measurement registration without its own description the first-priority config.description is that sentence and metadata.description is never reached. The demo's XRF, ICP-MS and example measurements therefore show the generic sentence in the operations, section and record description although their metadata has a specific one. Followed the order the task names; not changed.

Only the contributor's modified column is indexed (db_index=True). Project, dataset, sample and measurement modified are not, so modified_after/modified_before scan the table. No migration added, as instructed.

A tag name must be unique in the schema, so a sample type and a measurement type with the same plural name would share one section (the first registered wins). The routes already keep them apart; the demo has no such pair.

A viewset of a portal's own that is on the router but has no docstring of its own inherits BaseViewSet's developer-facing docstring in its operation descriptions (drf-spectacular reads it with inspect.getdoc). Its section carries no description. Not changed.

demo/config.py comments and docstrings still say metadata.description surfaces as the operation description; true only when config.description is empty (see first concern). Outside the story, untouched.
The modified filters take a date as the start of that day, and a time without an offset is read in the portal's time zone.
